observed_vs_expected: Expected observation 1 stated best_target_score should show a distinct convergence trajectory versus periodic routes if chirping helps. Instead, the route exhibits severe volatility: scores oscillate between 0.7072366782448362 (round 5) and 0.9830637191058961 (round 3) with no monotonic trend. Expected observation 2 stated tightest_margin should improve in stopband width compared to quarter-wave designs. The measured tightest_margin of 0.6122635821648035 does not demonstrate sustained improvement, and the trajectory remains erratic. Expected observation 3 predicted that if the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau lower or passband will split; the data supports partial failure — the score has regressed from its peak of 0.9830637191058961 to 0.7956004944063685 by round 8, indicating stagnation at a degraded level rather than clear passband splitting.
deviation_mechanism: Chirped layer stacks break the translational symmetry that gives quarter-wave Bragg reflectors their robust, slowly-varying spectral response. Each additional thickness degree of freedom introduces an independent optical-phase term φ_i = 4π n_i d_i / λ. Because d_i varies continuously rather than repeating every two layers, the reflection coefficient becomes a superposition of many quasi-resonant cavities with spacing δλ ≈ λ²/(2 n_eff Δd). This produces narrow transmission ripples separated by sub-nanometer gaps, yielding a highly multimodal objective landscape with deep local minima. Gradient-based optimizers cannot traverse these barriers efficiently, resulting in the observed score oscillation (0.707 → 0.906 → 0.731 → 0.796 across rounds 5–8) as the solver alternates between trapped local configurations rather than converging to a global optimum.
continue_rationale: Eight rounds have been executed. The peak score of 0.9830637191058961 in round 3 proves the chirped topology can reach high-performance configurations when initialized appropriately. Subsequent degradation (to 0.7956004944063685 by round 8) reflects optimizer entrapment rather than physical infeasibility. Since viable regions of thickness space exist, a revised initialization and optimizer strategy can access them. Continuing is scientifically warranted to determine whether constrained chirp ranges recover the lost performance.

insight_grounding: The round-3 best candidate (candidate index 2, tied among three top performers) achieved score 0.9830637191058961 with thickness values including layers at 220.80 nm, 185.45 nm, 337.40 nm, and 303.58 nm — a moderate chirp spread of roughly 35% around the quarter-wave center. By contrast, round-8 candidates exhibit pathological layer assignments: candidate 3 (index 2) contains alternating extremes of 82.11 nm and 392.74 nm (layers 4 and 3 respectively), producing destructive phase cancellation confirmed by the score collapse to 0.7072366782448362 in round 5. The regression from 0.9830637191058961 to 0.7956004944063685 over five rounds (rounds 3→8) demonstrates that unconstrained chirp exploration destabilizes the solution, whereas the earlier successful round-3 configuration validates the underlying material stack.
